sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Immunological synapse formation evaluated in SVT2 cells (L1); TDB-mediated killing assay confirmed surface display of the gD epitope on cells expressing the tagged full-length construct (L3); construct was functional in both assays.
sites.rationale: All three ledger lines describe the same membrane-anchored FCRL5 construct bearing an N-terminal gD epitope tag. The signal peptide (residues 1–15) is cleaved co-translationally, so the tag must be inserted after residue 15 to remain on the extracellular face; placing it upstream would result in silent cleavage. Python confirms seq[14]='G' (residue 15) and seq[15]='Q' (residue 16), and the tag sits 832 residues from the TM boundary (848), well clear of any constraint. The C-terminus is intracellular, making this the only extracellular terminus and the position unambiguous by topology. Full-length FCRL5 with an N-terminal gD expression tag was expressed in SVT2 cells via retrovirus (L1) and in a lentiviral vector as an FcRH5-mRuby2 fusion (L2); surface display of the gD epitope was confirmed in TDB killing assays (L3). No residue number is stated in any clip; the signal peptide spans residues 1–15 and the mature N-terminus begins at residue 16 (Q), making this the sole extracellular terminus. The junction is therefore computed as insert_after_residue=15 (G|Q).

sources.claim: To evaluate the immunological synapse formation, SVT2 cells were infected with retrovirus encoding full-length FcRH5 with N-terminal gD expression tag or truncated FcRH5 (deletion of AA1-744) with N-terminal gD tag.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) ground the same single site: the N-terminal gD epitope tag on full-length membrane-anchored FCRL5, placed after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 15. No ledger line names a specific residue number; the junction is topology-derived from the signal-peptide landmark. L2 additionally describes a C-terminal mRuby2 fusion, but the C-terminus of FCRL5 is intracellular (residues 870–977) and therefore not a surface tag site; it is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal loop insertion.

literature_other_positions.note: mRuby2 fluorescent protein was fused to the C-terminus of FCRL5 in the pHR-FcRH5-mRuby2 lentiviral construct; the C-terminus (residues 870–977) is intracellular and not accessible for extracellular surface tagging.
